purpose.statement: Media helps people understand, create, restore, enhance, edit, animate, simulate, synchronize, compose, assess, and deliver governed audio, video, image, speech, spatial, and time-based work. Users can move from intent to reviewable output while retaining source material, seeing material changes, and understanding what is measured, estimated, reconstructed, generated, or unknown. Media does not claim the domain authority of a scientific, pedagogical, clinical, rights, or publication owner.
purpose.forWhom: Canonical actor records: media.creator, media.editor, media.reviewer, media.developer-integrator, media.automation-client, media.operator, media.administrator, media.privacy-rights-reviewer, media.worker, media.external-provider, media.domain-reviewer.

scope.description: The intended Media product scope spans understanding, creation, restoration, enhancement, editing, animation, simulation, synchronization, composition, mastering, quality assessment, and delivery of governed media. Inclusion in this scope defines product meaning; it does not assert that a capability is implemented, licensed, qualified, or available in any runtime.
inclusions: image, video, audio, and music creation
media-specific visual recognition and temporal/scene-text semantics
exclusions: generic Document Intelligence/OCR runtime and parser providers
generic model/provider router, credentials, quota, and failover
generic identity, workflow, audit, observability, and product-development frameworks
Data Cloud governed metadata/read-model and compatibility ownership
pedagogical truth, clinical decisions, campaign claims, and scientific model authority
external provider certification and legal/rights determinations
Explorer simulations as evidence of production runtime behavior

nonGoals.description: Media will not implement or own generic document OCR, extraction, parser or document-management engines.
nonGoals.reason: MDI-001 assigns their public contracts to Shared and runtime execution to Document Intelligence; Media owns temporal scene-text mappings only.

nonGoals.description: Media will not create competing identity, authorization, workflow, event, audit, observability, governance or generic AI routing frameworks.
nonGoals.reason: Public Ghatana Shared and platform contracts own these mechanics; Media supplies domain-specific intent and adapters.

nonGoals.description: Media will not own a competing product-definition, Explorer, evidence or Lifecycle closure framework.
nonGoals.reason: Ghatana Tools and Lifecycle own the public schemas, generic host mechanics, proof admission and receipts.

nonGoals.description: Media presentation and simulation will not claim independent clinical, pedagogical, scientific or rights adjudication.
nonGoals.reason: Specialized domain owners and verified external authorities retain the meaning and approval of such claims.

nonGoals.description: Media will not promise every codec, model, voice, hardware profile, provider or format to be universally licensed, qualified or available.
nonGoals.reason: Implementation, model or asset licensing, technical qualification and profile availability are independent admission dimensions.

actors.name: creator
actors.description: Turn an idea, brief, or source material into a governed media result. May initiate only actions authorized for the current identity and project; creation intent is not a license grant, privacy exception, or publication approval.
responsibilities: Express intent and review proposed inputs, constraints, and material tradeoffs.
Supply or select source material only within applicable rights and access policy.
Review and accept outputs where the workflow requires creator acceptance.

actors.name: editor
actors.description: Make controlled, reviewable changes while preserving source material and accepted revisions. Editing authority is limited to the selected project and authorized assets; an edit or local approval does not reverse a completed external publication.
responsibilities: Edit through versioned, non-destructive operations.
Review changed regions, timing, quality, and provenance before accepting a revision.

actors.name: reviewer
actors.description: Decide whether an exact version meets its stated review purpose. Review authority is purpose- and scope-limited. A review does not imply rights clearance, scientific validation, or publication permission unless separately assigned and authorized.
responsibilities: Review the version, context, evidence, and requested review criteria.
Record a decision that remains bound to that exact version and purpose.

actors.name: developer integrator
actors.description: Integrate Media through supported contracts and maintain compatible clients and workflows. Integration access is controlled by credentials and scopes; developer status does not authorize access to customer content or production effects.
responsibilities: Use documented public APIs, SDKs, CLI contracts, and integration boundaries.
Surface contract errors and finality without inventing product state.

actors.name: automation client
actors.description: Automate repeatable, declared media workflows with inspectable inputs and outcomes. Automation inherits only its scoped machine identity and delegated policy; it cannot infer a retry-safe outcome from timeout or lost observation.
responsibilities: Submit bounded requests through the public API/SDK/CLI contract.
Preserve idempotency, cancellation, and unknown-finality semantics.

actors.name: operator
actors.description: Maintain service operation and help resolve blocked or degraded work safely. Operational access does not grant content rights or permission to alter customer assets, bypass product policy, or claim a job outcome without evidence.
responsibilities: Inspect health, bounded diagnostics, queue/service state, and safe recovery options.
Preserve job, audit, and artifact finality while responding to incidents.

actors.name: administrator
actors.description: Configure approved product and tenant settings within assigned scope. Administrative status is scoped and policy-derived; it does not imply unrestricted access to media contents, rights, approval, or external publication.
responsibilities: Apply reviewed configuration and manage scoped identities/settings.
Keep configuration changes auditable and reversible where safe.

actors.name: privacy rights reviewer
actors.description: Assess whether a processing or lifecycle decision respects privacy, consent, retention, and rights obligations. Review conclusions are advisory or gating only as defined by an assigned policy/approval contract; review does not invent legal rights or waive policy.
responsibilities: Review relevant processing purpose, data flow, consent, rights, retention, and deletion implications.
Identify required approvals or unresolved policy conditions before a consequential effect.

actors.name: worker
actors.description: Execute the admitted processing step and preserve traceable, bounded results. A worker is not a user or approver. It must not widen its plan, silently downgrade quality or policy, or use generic document-intelligence internals.
responsibilities: Validate its scoped inputs and plan, enforce resource/cancellation bounds, and report outputs and failures.
Preserve provenance and avoid unauthorized side effects.

actors.name: external provider
actors.description: Complete only the provider operation requested under an admitted contract. A provider is not an authority for Media product semantics, rights, quality acceptance, approval, or final external effects.
responsibilities: Return contract-defined result, error, provenance, and execution identity where supported.
Honor the admitted data-processing and execution boundary.

A relevant domain owner must appoint the reviewer and define the evidence basis; no scientific, clinical, pedagogical, legal, or safety conclusion is implied without the applicable owner contract.
responsibilities: Identify the relevant domain authority and scope for a review.
Assess declared assumptions and evidence only within the assigned domain scope.

userIntents.intent: Create a new governed media result from intent, a brief, source material, or an admitted recipe.
Restore or enhance while preserving source and exposing material reconstruction or quality tradeoffs.
Change media through versioned, reviewable operations.
Create time-varying visual media as a first-class animation workflow.
Run or present a declared simulation/procedural workflow with explicit fidelity boundaries.
Inspect media and derive audio, speech, visual, or scene observations for a declared use.
Prepare, export, or publish an authorized output to a declared destination.
Review or change authorized user and workspace settings with their effective scope, owner, inheritance, and effects on active work.
Review, comment on, approve, reject, or request changes for an immutable version within an explicit scope and assigned authority.
Find task-specific Media guidance and safe next steps; preview and redact diagnostics before explicitly sharing them.
Archive, restore, branch, and recover a versioned project while preserving revision history, current access policy, and source lineage.
Inspect and manage artifact retention, revocation, and erasure with explicit scope, copy-level evidence, and truthful external-control limits.
View status, check an uncertain outcome, stop, retry, or recover a job without replaying unknown external effects or weakening policy.
Recover or close a live media session after disconnect, lease loss, cancellation, or uncertain frame processing while preserving ordering and consent boundaries.
Choose an eligible processing option after reviewing its requirements, limitations, and compatible bindings; the choice does not imply runtime availability.
Check available processing options and execution compatibility while distinguishing contract, license, qualification, and runtime status.
Check scoped service readiness and degradation using bounded, authorized diagnostics without exposing unrelated tenant or content details.
Review purpose-bound rights and consent evidence, including revocation and expiry, with the responsible authority; do not treat user assertion as verification.
Inspect source lineage, transformations, origin disclosures, retention, and erasure evidence for an exact artifact or project version.

businessIntents.description: Integrating products reuse public governed Media capabilities without creating incompatible per-product media execution authorities.
Reviewers and integrating products can distinguish originals, exact derived versions, uncertainty and authorized delivery.
Processing execution has declared supported profiles with controlled policy, budget, resource and failure behavior.
Long-running jobs remain observable and safely reconcilable without blind replay or misleading cancellation outcomes.

desiredOutcomes.description: Produce a useful media asset that satisfies the user's declared intent and constraints.
Improve or transform media without losing the original bytes or accepted project revisions.
Find and use relevant audio, visual, speech, and scene information from media for a declared purpose.
Communicate an idea through composed, animated, or simulated media while preserving domain-owner truth.
Restore or enhance a source while making material reconstruction, quality, and identity tradeoffs inspectable.
Review an exact version and its relevant quality, rights, provenance, and approval evidence.
Deliver or publish an approved output through an authorized destination and declared effect boundary.
Invoke Media through a stable public contract and reconcile work without inventing parallel state.
Understand and resolve a blocked or degraded operation without weakening policy or losing eligible work.
Apply authorized user preferences and workspace policies while preserving shared authority and access boundaries.

capabilities.name: Create project
capabilities.description: A project named by the required non-empty title is represented as versioned project state. The definition does not say that the project starts empty or contains any particular assets.

capabilities.name: Inspect project
capabilities.description: The selected versioned project's state is returned for inspection; this is an observation and does not change project state.

capabilities.name: Update project
capabilities.description: The requested project update is reflected in returned versioned project state. The specific fields and resulting values are determined by the user intent and are not enumerated by this definition.

capabilities.name: Search projects
capabilities.description: A search over the caller's authorized project scope returns a bounded result page and, when applicable, an opaque continuation token. The requested page size is 1–100.

capabilities.name: Organize projects
capabilities.description: The project is organized according to the declared user intent, with the resulting project state returned. The definition does not specify organizational fields or a hierarchy.

capabilities.name: Archive project
capabilities.description: The requested project is archived and its resulting versioned project state is returned. Archiving does not by itself mean deletion or remote-copy removal.

capabilities.name: Version project
capabilities.description: Intended result: represent the requested project versioning in the returned versioned project state. Whether the intent creates, commits, or selects a version is not specified.

capabilities.name: Duplicate project
capabilities.description: A distinct project copy is created from the selected project, with versioned project state returned. Which contents, history, or access settings the copy carries is not defined.

capabilities.name: Branch project
capabilities.description: A project branch is produced from the selected versioned project and returned as versioned project state. The starting revision and branch contents are not specified by the current request shape.

capabilities.name: Collaborate on project
capabilities.description: Intended result: a collaboration outcome for the project, represented in versioned project state and, when the intent concerns participation, project-membership state. The participant and the particular collaboration change are not specified.

capabilities.name: Review project
capabilities.description: The result records a comment, approval, rejection, or request for changes for one exact immutable project version, within an explicit purpose and one or more selected review scopes (quality, rights, provenance, or approval), and only under current assigned reviewer authority with an explicit scope and expiry disposition. The review outcome remains linked to that exact version and scope; it does not mutate the reviewed version, clear rights, or authorize external publication. Missing or stale version, scope, purpose, evidence, authority, or expiry disposition leaves the result UNKNOWN or blocks the review.

capabilities.name: Restore project
capabilities.description: Intended result: restore the versioned project while preserving revision history, current access policy, and source lineage, as required by the linked restore-project intent. The particular historical revision is not specified.

capabilities.name: Attach source asset
capabilities.description: Intended result: associate a source asset with the project. The asset identity and version, and the exact project relation, are not specified by this leaf.

capabilities.name: Attach derived asset
capabilities.description: Intended result: associate a derived asset with the project. The asset identity and version, lineage, and exact project relation are not specified by this leaf.

capabilities.name: Update project composition
capabilities.description: Intended result: update the project composition according to the declared user intent, with versioned project state as the defined output. The composition representation and changed fields are unspecified.

capabilities.name: Update project settings
capabilities.description: Intended result: update project settings according to the declared user intent, with versioned project state as the defined output. Setting names, effective scope, inheritance, policy owner, and effects on active work are unspecified.

capabilities.name: Ingest artifact
capabilities.description: The result represents ingest from exactly one declared source-media or project-reference input with rights-and-retention context, as a governed artifact reference or lifecycle observation. A supplied reference alone does not establish that source material was consumed or create source-derived lineage.

capabilities.name: Upload artifact
capabilities.description: The result represents acknowledged bytes for one authorized source under a stable upload identity; verification is a separate step before an artifact version is available.

capabilities.name: Resume upload
capabilities.description: The result represents continuation of one existing authorized upload from owner-confirmed transfer state, with its upload identity unchanged and progress reported no further than confirmed.

capabilities.name: Import artifact
capabilities.description: The result represents resolution of an admitted source reference or staged upload and creation of a governed Media artifact version only after source-authority and integrity requirements are satisfied.

capabilities.name: Inspect artifact
capabilities.description: The result is the authorized status and recorded metadata for one exact immutable artifact version. Inspection is observational and does not modify bytes, project membership, or rights.

capabilities.name: Search artifacts
capabilities.description: The result is a bounded page of governed artifact records for exactly one supplied source-media or project reference under rights-and-retention context, with required pageSize (1–100) and optional opaque pageToken. Search fields, criteria, matching, ordering, and completeness are unspecified.

capabilities.name: List artifacts
capabilities.description: The result is a bounded enumeration page of governed artifact records for exactly one supplied source-media or project reference under rights-and-retention context, with required pageSize (1–100) and optional opaque pageToken. Ordering, total count, and completeness are unspecified.

capabilities.name: Download artifact
capabilities.description: The result for download is the governed artifact reference or lifecycle observation associated with exactly one supplied source-media or project reference under rights-and-retention context. This output does not establish that bytes were transferred or verified.

capabilities.name: Derive artifact
capabilities.description: The P0 meaning of a derivation result is bound to exact source-version references, transformation-profile identity, requested output/media type, purpose, and rights decision. Distinguish a queued-job observation from derived content and derived content from a registered artifact-version identity; exact source lineage is required and an identified profile is not an assumed default. Unknown source, authority, or result remains UNKNOWN. This P0 meaning does not establish dispatch, job creation, persistence, derived content, registration, or completion.

capabilities.name: Register output
capabilities.description: The P0 meaning of output registration distinguishes the supplied candidate from an immutable Media artifact-version identity, an accepted registration result from rejected or unknown outcomes, and registration from project attachment, export, delivery, or publication. Candidate lineage, content digest, policy decision, and target project revision are identity constraints; a registered version is not inferred from the request. This P0 meaning does not establish mutation, registration, persistence, or finality.

capabilities.name: Share artifact
capabilities.description: The result is a sharing-grant observation for one governed artifact reference and one recipient/sharing scope under rights-and-retention context, when applicable authority permits that scope. A grant observation does not establish recipient access or download.

capabilities.name: Revoke artifact sharing
capabilities.description: The result is a revocation observation, confirmed or unknown, for either one exact sharing-grant reference or one artifact-recipient scope under rights-and-retention context. Revocation of a grant does not establish recall or erasure of copies already obtained.

capabilities.name: Delete artifact
capabilities.description: The result is the lifecycle observation for one governed artifact reference under rights-and-retention context. Keep access revocation, hold-blocked, erasure pending, confirmed erasure, and external-erasure uncertainty distinct where recorded; do not infer external-copy recall.

capabilities.name: Retain artifact
capabilities.description: The result is the governed artifact reference or lifecycle observation for exactly one source-media or project reference under rights-and-retention context. The leaf specifies no retention duration, selected policy, or physical-storage guarantee.

capabilities.name: Export provenance
capabilities.description: The result is the governed artifact reference or lifecycle observation for a provenance export using the specified expected source-version references, destination reference, and versioned delivery profile under rights-and-retention context. The output does not define package encoding or establish transport or destination acknowledgement.

capabilities.name: Resolve source reference
capabilities.description: The result is the governed artifact reference or lifecycle observation associated with exactly one supplied source-media or project reference under rights-and-retention context. Resolution alone does not establish import, registration, byte consumption, or source-derived lineage.

capabilities.name: Submit job
capabilities.description: A successful submit result identifies one accepted operation request as a Media job reference and admission observation; acceptance alone does not establish work execution or output production.

capabilities.name: View job status
capabilities.description: Return a tenant-authorized snapshot of one Media job’s status dimensions and currently indicated safe next actions.

capabilities.name: List jobs
capabilities.description: Return a bounded, authorized page of Media jobs matching the caller’s declared filters.

capabilities.name: Watch job
capabilities.description: Observe one authorized Media job through bounded polling or an admitted resumable event stream.

capabilities.name: Cancel job
capabilities.description: Request cancellation of an authorized Media job and report whether the request, stop, or final cancellation is confirmed.

capabilities.name: Retry job
capabilities.description: Start one newly authorized, bounded attempt within the same logical Media job when retry policy permits it.

capabilities.name: Check job outcome
capabilities.description: Resolve the certainty and safe next action for one existing Media job from stable owner evidence.

capabilities.name: Inspect job outputs
capabilities.description: Return a bounded, authorized page of one Media job’s output references with a per-output disposition.

capabilities.name: Inspect bounded execution history
capabilities.description: Return a bounded, redacted history of commands, attempts, and transitions for one authorized Media job.

capabilities.name: Open stream session
capabilities.description: On admitted request, ask the governed session owner to open the requested stream and return the typed ordered-stream observation or terminal session state. This records the owner’s response; it does not establish media quality, clock accuracy, or end-to-end delivery.

capabilities.name: Connect stream session
capabilities.description: Request connection of the identified stream session under the supplied consent and capability context; return only the owner-observed ordered stream/session state.

capabilities.name: Submit stream frame
capabilities.description: Submit the requested frame within the admitted stream session and return the owner-observed ordered stream/session result; an invocation result is not proof of downstream consumption.

capabilities.name: Acknowledge stream frame
capabilities.description: Record or request acknowledgement for a frame in its stream session and return the stream owner’s ordered state observation.

capabilities.name: Close stream session
capabilities.description: Request closure of the identified governed session and return the owner-observed terminal or nonterminal session state.

capabilities.name: Reconnect stream session
capabilities.description: Request reconnection of a previously identified session under current consent and capability context; return the owner-observed session state.

capabilities.name: Enforce stream ordering
capabilities.description: Apply the declared ordering rule to stream events/frames and return an observation of ordering handling from the session owner.

capabilities.name: Renew a stream connection lease
capabilities.description: Represent a bounded lease-renewal intent for an admitted stream connection after the current token and consent are checked; report lease/session state only from owner evidence.

capabilities.name: Bound stream buffers
capabilities.description: Apply the declared finite buffer bounds to the admitted stream and return the observed buffer/session disposition.

capabilities.name: Apply bounded backpressure to a stream
capabilities.description: Represent a bounded backpressure intent for a lagging stream consumer within the declared buffer/session limits, with the resulting stream observation or terminal session state reported when known.

capabilities.name: Integrate stream recording
capabilities.description: Request governed recording integration for the identified stream and return the ordered stream observation or terminal state from the owning session/recording boundary.

capabilities.name: Integrate live processing
capabilities.description: Request governed live-processing integration for the stream under its admitted capability and consent context; return the observed stream/session state.

capabilities.name: Deliver live media over WebRTC
capabilities.description: Represent a request to use WebRTC for live media transport and return an owner-reported stream observation or terminal session state when known.

capabilities.name: Deliver live media with adaptive HTTP streaming
capabilities.description: Represent a request to use adaptive HTTP live-media transport and return an owner-reported stream observation or terminal session state when known.

capabilities.name: Deliver live media over HLS
capabilities.description: Represent a request to use HLS live-media transport and return an owner-reported stream observation or terminal session state when known.

capabilities.name: Deliver live media over DASH
capabilities.description: Represent a request to use DASH live-media transport and return an owner-reported stream observation or terminal session state when known.

capabilities.name: Enable live captions
capabilities.description: Request live caption integration for the identified stream and return the owner-observed ordered stream/session state; any caption text is only a separately typed output if provided by the authoritative boundary.

capabilities.name: Choose an eligible processing option
capabilities.description: Discover declared profile definitions and return the exact profile/catalog observation supported by the source; discovery reports declarations and does not admit execution.

capabilities.name: Check media delivery compatibility
capabilities.description: Evaluate one named output profile against an explicit outcome and input constraints, returning per-dimension compatibility and blockers without executing delivery.

capabilities.name: Discover declared capabilities
capabilities.description: Discover declared capability leaves and their source-declared metadata, returning an observation of the requested catalog scope.

capabilities.name: Check declared processing options
capabilities.description: A caller can check declared processing options and their capability evidence; current runtime readiness remains a separate check.

capabilities.name: Check execution compatibility
capabilities.description: Compare a declared capability query with the requested operation and profile, returning a declared-capability-and-compatibility result as an observation only.

capabilities.name: Inspect capability-scoped readiness
capabilities.description: Inspect readiness for the requested capability scope and return a capability-scoped readiness observation, preserving the boundary and source of each observed check.

capabilities.name: Resolve consent reference
capabilities.description: Resolve the supplied rights evidence reference in the given identity/authority context and return exactly one source-declared result variant: POLICY_DECISION_REFERENCE or RIGHTS_OBSERVATION. Preserve the variant selector and referenced evidence as supplied.

capabilities.name: Evaluate permitted use
capabilities.description: Evaluate the supplied rights evidence reference in the given identity/authority context and return exactly the source-declared POLICY_DECISION_REFERENCE or RIGHTS_OBSERVATION variant, without reconstructing or translating the variant.

capabilities.name: Record rights attestation
capabilities.description: Record an asserted rights attestation for the supplied identity/authority context and rights-evidence reference as the declared asserted-rights-attestation-record; the record represents the attestation made, not independent verification of the asserted right.

capabilities.name: Inspect source lineage
capabilities.description: Inspect source lineage for the selected artifact or execution reference and return a minimized provenance record/disclosure containing only source links supported by authoritative evidence.

capabilities.name: Inspect execution lineage
capabilities.description: Inspect execution lineage for the selected artifact or execution reference and disclose only execution, adapter/profile, and version facts present in authoritative records.

capabilities.name: Disclose origin
capabilities.description: Disclose the origin of the selected artifact or execution reference using only available authored-intent or source-derived provenance evidence.

capabilities.name: Record retention effect
capabilities.description: Create a minimized local candidate/draft provenance record of the observed retention effect for the supplied artifact or execution reference; this capability does not itself change canonical retention state.

capabilities.name: Record erasure effect
capabilities.description: Create a minimized local candidate/draft provenance record of the observed erasure effect for the supplied artifact or execution reference; this does not perform erasure or establish deletion at external systems.

capabilities.name: Track public-DI text regions across frames
capabilities.description: Track OCR/D.I.-supplied text regions across declared video frames or frame references, retaining region and time association as a scene-text observation. The result remains a reviewable analysis candidate or observation, and any source-derived relation or lineage is asserted only when actual source consumption and linkage are established.

capabilities.name: Create timestamped scene-text observation from public-DI results
capabilities.description: Represent a timestamped scene-text observation from the declared public Document Intelligence result and video/frame context. The result remains a reviewable analysis candidate or observation, and any source-derived relation or lineage is asserted only when actual source consumption and linkage are established.

capabilities.name: Transcribe audio file
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is file transcription represented by a tracking reference and, if produced, an unverified transcript draft linked to source version/timebase with provided language or recognition evidence.

capabilities.name: Transcribe audio stream
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is the intent to obtain speech transcription or analysis for a declared audio artifact/live-stream input, with timing and uncertainty where supplied.

capabilities.name: Detect language
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is language detection as a language observation associated with speech/audio analysis.

capabilities.name: Detect voice activity
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is voice-activity detection as temporal observations of voice activity in audio.

capabilities.name: Diarize speakers
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is diarization as assigning speech portions to distinct within-recording speaker labels/turns when evidence is provided.

capabilities.name: Segment speakers
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is speaker segmentation as dividing speech into speaker-associated segments.

capabilities.name: Separate speakers in a transcript
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is separation of speakers in transcript analysis as distinguishing speaker-associated transcript portions.

capabilities.name: Identify authorized speaker
capabilities.description: Authorized-speaker identification may produce an estimated or inferred speaker observation only against the required versioned authorized-speaker-reference and when current purpose-specific consent and policy permit comparison. It does not assert identity ground truth; otherwise it abstains or remains UNKNOWN.

capabilities.name: Create word timestamps
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is creation of word-level timing observations associated with recognized speech.

capabilities.name: Create phoneme timestamps
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is creation of phoneme-level timing observations associated with speech.

capabilities.name: Match transcript timing to audio
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is alignment of a supplied transcript version to a supplied authorized audio version as a candidate, returning qualified segment/word timing observations and limitations/provenance where available.

capabilities.name: Punctuate and capitalize transcript
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is punctuation and capitalization as text formatting of a transcript.

capabilities.name: Provide transcription alternatives
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is provision of alternative transcription candidates for ambiguous speech.

capabilities.name: Provide confidence information
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is confidence information associated with transcription or speech-analysis results.

capabilities.name: Translate speech
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is translation of speech content as a translated transcript/analysis result.

capabilities.name: Generate subtitles
capabilities.description: The P0 result meaning is a subtitle draft with timing/alignment disposition and source/operation provenance.

capabilities.name: Detect visual entities
capabilities.description: Describe requested visual entity detection as a typed analysis result for the declared image/video analysis request. The result remains a reviewable analysis candidate or observation, and any source-derived relation or lineage is asserted only when actual source consumption and linkage are established.

capabilities.name: Classify visual entities
capabilities.description: Describe requested visual entity classification as a typed analysis result for the declared image/video analysis request. The result remains a reviewable analysis candidate or observation, and any source-derived relation or lineage is asserted only when actual source consumption and linkage are established.

capabilities.name: Segment image
capabilities.description: Describe requested image segmentation as a typed analysis result for image regions or masks. The result remains a reviewable analysis candidate or observation, and any source-derived relation or lineage is asserted only when actual source consumption and linkage are established.

capabilities.name: Segment video
capabilities.description: Describe requested video segmentation as a typed analysis result with frame/time-scoped regions or masks. The result remains a reviewable analysis candidate or observation, and any source-derived relation or lineage is asserted only when actual source consumption and linkage are established.

capabilities.name: Track objects
capabilities.description: Describe requested object tracking as a typed visual analysis result associating detected regions across the declared temporal scope. The result remains a reviewable analysis candidate or observation, and any source-derived relation or lineage is asserted only when actual source consumption and linkage are established.

capabilities.name: Track points

All input, decoding, import, model, scene, shader, script, and archive processing is bounded and isolated before content is promoted to trusted usable state.
Tenant, classification, consent, purpose, residency, egress, provider-retention, training, and rights remain independent policy axes at every applicable processing boundary.
Required external effects have durable accountable intent before dispatch; uncertain effects are never replayed merely to repair missing evidence.
Operational logs, traces, metrics, audit, and provenance have distinct schemas and retention; redaction failure never falls back to raw sensitive content.
Every supported task is keyboard operable with visible focus and non-drag alternatives; screen-reader output exposes selected media objects, measurements, status, and permitted actions.
UI locale, speech language, subtitle language, voice locale, and metadata/time formatting are independent; unsupported languages are declared unavailable rather than silently substituted.
The primary experience is intent-first with progressive disclosure; expert controls and provider details do not burden ordinary users or hide consequential choices.
Control-plane and local interaction performance is measured separately from external model, render, simulation, and encoding work on frozen reference environments.

Every job and optimization must have finite CPU, system-memory, video-memory, GPU-time, storage, network-transfer, process-count, wall-time, retry-count, and monetary bounds for each applicable dimension before dispatch; an unknown or unevaluated applicable bound blocks admission, and each fallback rechecks budget and quality authority.
Sample, frame, clip, and event timestamps use explicit rational clocks and declared rounding/resampling rules with no silent drift.
Scientific/domain fidelity is separate from visual quality; quality measures state applicability and abstention, and never override rights or domain constraints.
Restart, retry, cancellation, restore, and reconciliation preserve identity, idempotency, fences, erasure tombstones, and uncertainty.

Local-development, private-local, connected-production, and hybrid-production are explicit capability-scoped contracts; no profile silently enables network egress, model download, or a lower-fidelity fallback.
Production SLO, RPO, RTO, restore, and soak limits are owner-approved and backed by deployment-specific observation before activation.

domainRules.name: Machine-scoped state identity
domainRules.rule: A state identifier is meaningful only together with its machine; equal spellings across job, attempt, upload, stream, or delivery machines do not establish equivalent state or behavior.
domainRules.rationale: Preserve the owner-adjudicated machine-scoped identity rule and reject lossy cross-machine normalization.

domainRules.name: Request receipt is not queued execution
domainRules.rule: A request receipt or ACCEPTED response proves receipt only; it does not prove durable queueing, worker claim, dispatch, or execution.
domainRules.rationale: Keep ingress acknowledgment distinct from job state and attempt execution.

domainRules.name: Unknown outcome remains unresolved
domainRules.rule: OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is neither running nor failure nor safe-to-retry; preserve uncertainty until an authoritative reconciliation resolves the effect.
domainRules.rationale: Prevent a lossy observation from authorizing duplicate external effects.

domainRules.name: Completion is distinct from delivery acknowledgment
domainRules.rule: A completed job requires the operation-defined output set, integrity, authority, and durable result commit; it does not establish recipient delivery acknowledgment.
domainRules.rationale: Keep result finality separate from external delivery evidence.

domainRules.name: Cancellation requires authoritative finality
domainRules.rule: A cancellation request or observer detachment does not establish cancellation; cancellation requires authoritative no-dispatch or confirmed fenced-effects finality under the operation contract.
domainRules.rationale: Keep request intent and observed cancellation result distinct.

domainRules.name: Partial success requires closed effect accounting
domainRules.rule: PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED is terminal only when every declared sub-effect has an explicit closed disposition and no consequential effect remains unknown.
domainRules.rationale: Prevent unresolved effects from being hidden by an aggregate partial-success label.

invariants.statement: A private context does not imply local processing, and local processing does not imply authorized use.
invariants.violation: If processing locality or authorization is missing or conflicting, return blocked or review-required; make no locality claim without a binding and observation.

invariants.statement: User attestation is not verified consent or license.
invariants.violation: Do not admit governed processing or distribution when required consent or license evidence is absent, expired, revoked, or unverified; return blocked or review-required with the reason.

invariants.statement: Source classification is a floor for derived data until an authorized deidentification promotion.
invariants.violation: Do not persist or promote metadata whose classification, tenant ownership, retention, or provenance checks fail.

invariants.statement: Model-generated content or assertions cannot authorize themselves.
invariants.violation: Reject model output as approval or privileged authority; require current policy and a separately authorized decision at the effect boundary.

invariants.statement: Required audit intent must be recorded before crossing an external effect boundary.
invariants.violation: Do not dispatch or publish when required audit intent cannot be recorded; if an effect may already have occurred, preserve outcome uncertainty and do not replay to repair the audit record.

invariants.statement: Policy revocation stops future dispatch and restricts outputs at the next enforcement point.
invariants.violation: Re-check current authority at effect boundaries; stop future dispatch and restrict outputs when policy has been revoked, without claiming an in-flight effect was terminated.

invariants.statement: Cross-tenant access and reuse are denied.
invariants.violation: Deny read, reuse, or effect when tenant ownership does not match the verified request context, even when content digests match.

journeys.name: First use, authentication, context, and project creation
steps: Authenticate through the admitted identity contract and select an authorized tenant/workspace.
A versioned empty project exists and the creator sees a safe next action without selecting a provider/model/engine.

journeys.name: Upload/import, inspect, and produce a usable artifact
steps: Source selection and upload are authorized; current consent/retention rules are checked.
Original bytes remain identifiable and an artifact version has integrity and available technical metadata recorded.

journeys.name: Audio/video transcription through corrected captions
steps: Audio/video access, language intent, and required consent/processing policy are available.
Timestamped transcript/caption draft is reviewable with language, timing, provenance, uncertainty, and exact source version.

journeys.name: Authorized text-to-speech to approved audio
steps: Text, voice rights/consent, language and output intent are admitted.
A reviewable audio artifact records selected voice/version, format/rate, provenance, and approval status where required.

journeys.name: Image/video analysis, geometry, and tracks
steps: Source and analysis purpose are authorized; technical input limits are explicit.
Observations retain source artifact, timestamp/frame/region, model provenance, and confidence/uncertainty.

journeys.name: Multimodal or document consumer request to grounded typed result
steps: Consumer purpose and artifact access are authorized; Media-specific scene-text intent is distinguished from document extraction.
A typed result returns source/time/region/provenance and explicit uncertainty; generic document parsing remains with Document Intelligence.

journeys.name: Noisy/clipped interview cleanup with preservation and comparison
steps: Source and requested preservation profile are admitted.
A derived output and before/after comparison disclose processing and reconstruction limits.

journeys.name: Low-quality video repair with measured comparison
steps: The exact P0 repair capability, input envelope, profile constraints, and finite budget are defined; runtime operation admission remains a downstream check.
Eligible stabilized/upscaled/repaired output is compared under applicable metrics with limitations visible.

journeys.name: Prompt/brief to storyboard, composition, render, review, and delivery
steps: Intent, source/reference rights, budget, quality/preservation choices, and required reviewers are explicit.
Exact output version is reviewed, approved as required, and delivered with an accurate external-effect status.

journeys.name: Controlled generation with references and continuity review
steps: Reference/control uses are rights-checked; protected identity and geometry constraints are explicit.
Candidate sequence is reviewed for continuity with uncertainty/provenance exposed.

journeys.name: Region mask/tracking edit with comparison and undo
steps: Edit is bound to an exact artifact version, frame/time range, and authorized operation.
Region edit is versioned and reviewable; source and prior edit remain recoverable.

journeys.name: Deterministic 2D/vector/procedural animation
steps: Animation controls and exact timing/export subset are declared.
Accessible preview and export preserve declared curve/time semantics.

journeys.name: 3D character, rig, path, or control animation
steps: Scene/rig assets, coordinate convention, rights, and supported interchange subset are identified.
Render/export binds animation to a declared rig/scene version and reports conversion loss.

journeys.name: Explore a domain simulation and its measurements
steps: Domain owner/model, equations, unit-bearing conditions, validity range, solver envelope, and fidelity tier are referenced.
Measurements/passes and any animation/render remain traceable to domain model and declared fidelity.

journeys.name: Simulation/procedural passes with protected semantic validation
steps: Domain truth and protected semantic properties are identified before any generative refinement.
Refinement preserves accepted domain measurements or reports the exact failed validation and fidelity consequence.

journeys.name: Existing-video translation/dubbing and voice/timing review
steps: Source, translation intent, voice authority, subtitle/voice locales, and destination are independently specified.
Mastered version is synchronized, reviewed for meaning and timing, and delivered only with required approval.

journeys.name: Music, effects, Foley, stems, mix, and mastering
steps: Source/license scope, target profile, channel layout, and mastering intent are explicit.
Mix/master output records profile, loudness/peak measurements where applicable, and source lineage.

journeys.name: Compose clips, captions, exact graphics, color, and audio master
steps: Exact assets/fonts/brand claims, timeline mapping, color profile, and output destination are authorized.
Versioned composition renders with deterministic exact graphics and declared audiovisual/color profile.

journeys.name: Review media quality and improve it within declared limits
steps: Applicable metrics, thresholds, budget, stop conditions, and protected properties are defined.
User selects or declines a measurable successor candidate with estimated/reconstructed properties disclosed.

journeys.name: Observe a long-running job and check its outcome safely
steps: Job has stable request/attempt identity and durable status contract.
User observes completion or known uncertainty; cancellation/retry/reconciliation preserves completed work.

journeys.name: Review/comment/approve exact version and re-review changed material
steps: Review purpose, exact artifact version, reviewer authority, and scope/expiry are explicit.
Decision attaches to the reviewed version and required approval state.

journeys.name: Export/download/publish with destination acknowledgement
steps: Exact output, destination, rights, approval, and external-effect authority are current.
Package validity, transport, and external publication are reported as distinct finality outcomes.

journeys.name: Private/local workflow while disconnected and reconnect
steps: An admitted local capability, offline mode, cached asset permission, and storage policy are explicitly established.
Only work allowed in the admitted disconnected mode is completed; reconnect reconciles versions and jobs without remote fallback.

journeys.name: CLI batch/JSON plan through verified outputs
steps: Public command/request schema, explicit approval/policy input, client keys, and per-item budgets are accepted.
Each item reports its terminal/partial/unknown outcome and output refs using the same semantics as other channels.

journeys.name: Agent or product integration with bounded delegated Media action
steps: Public Media action, bounded authority/delegation, recursion/cost limits, and return contract are admitted.
Caller receives an opaque job/result reference and truthful status; any consequential effect has separate authority.

journeys.name: Delete/revoke/retention/hold and visible lifecycle
steps: Identity, deletion/revocation authority, retention/hold state, and affected artifact/derivative scope are resolved.
Product lifecycle reflects completion/partial/blocked status without claiming remote copies were recalled.

journeys.name: Continue safely when processing is unavailable
steps: Capability qualification, license, runtime availability, and fallback policy are checked independently.
User receives an admitted equivalent fallback with material differences disclosed or a clear blocked result.

journeys.name: Spatial/360/interactive/synthetic-data export to declared consumer
steps: Destination subset, coordinate/time conventions, synthetic-data labeling, and licensing are declared.
Consumer receives an identified package and conversion report with unsupported/lossy features disclosed.

journeys.name: Live session loss, consent change, and bounded recovery
steps: A live session has stable session/frame identity, bounded buffers, a current lease, and authoritative consent scope.
The session is confirmed closed/drained or its in-flight external effects remain explicitly unknown; no new frame crosses the boundary after revocation or fencing.

journeys.name: Check which processing options are eligible
steps: Identity, tenant/workspace scope, and diagnostic permissions are verified; profile, capability, provider, license, qualification, and runtime dimensions are represented separately.
The caller receives a bounded, current observation with provenance and explicit unknown/unsupported dimensions; an observation does not promise future availability.

contract.description: Eligible consumer workflows using versioned public contracts and preserved domain finality.
contract.populationEnumeration: Source applicability is enumerated per exact leaf; named admitted consumer/profile cohort and qualified observations remain NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.profileBinding: Freeze the release-profile ID and contract versions, selected exact capability leaves, deployment/region, tenant-policy scope, observation interval, and consumer cohort before counting. A fixture, candidate profile, or unversioned integration is not an admitted workflow.
contract.numerator: Count denominator workflows with a current public contract version and passing consumer conformance for every bound operation, including preserved idempotency, cancellation, status, and finality distinctions.
contract.denominator: Count distinct consumer workflows declared in the frozen release-profile cohort that invoke at least one bound public Media capability; retain failed, blocked, and untested workflows in the denominator. Exclude a workflow only when it is outside the declared cohort or no bound public capability applies, and record that reason.
contract.calculation: 100 * numerator / denominator; report percent and raw numerator/denominator integers. A zero denominator is NOT_APPLICABLE, never 100 percent; incomplete inventory or evidence is NOT_EVALUATED.
contract.valueUnit: percent; retain raw integer numerator and denominator with each observation.
contract.baselinePolicy: Establish only from a complete frozen cohort and observation interval using the same conformance oracle for every workflow; include failures and abstentions, preserve versioned evidence, and do not extrapolate from fixtures or request volume.
contract.targetPolicy: NOT_SET until Media owners select an explicit release-profile threshold after a qualified baseline and calibration review; do not assume 100 percent or transfer a target between profiles.
contract.applicability: Candidate workflows are those in the frozen consumer cohort that invoke at least one bound public Media capability. A current public contract version is required for the numerator; a missing or unadmitted contract leaves the workflow in the denominator but outside the numerator. Internal fixtures alone are not admitted consumer workflows.
contract.acceptanceCriterion: Every counted workflow identifies its contract version and has evidence that the consumer preserves the bound Media operation's finality distinctions.
contract.ownerRecommendation: Measure adoption as a distinct consumer-workflow conformance ratio, not call volume; repeated requests do not create additional workflows and a workflow with any failing bound operation does not enter the numerator.
contract.baseline: NOT_EVALUATED; no admitted consumer inventory is recorded by this product definition.
contract.target: NOT_SET; set only after a named release profile and qualified baseline are selected.
